findings: The analytic free-field denominator is deterministic and was previously validated against a numerical source-only BEM solve.

Exact reproduction of the worst scene gives identical listener positions, face indices, and obstacle vertices within 5e-9, but repeated BEM solves range from normal transfer around 1.7 to hundreds, while the stored result reaches 8.89e7.
The production solver uses a Burton-Miller boundary equation, so the failure is not explained by using a plain non-unique exterior integral equation.
The complex BiCGSTAB implementation uses torch.dot instead of Hermitian torch.vdot for rho, alpha, and omega.
BiCGSTAB silently returns its last iterate after 500 steps even when the relative residual is far above tolerance; the non-convergence warning is commented out.
Observed relative residuals for spiking production-style solves range from 4.8e-3 to 1.96e2, despite an intended relative norm tolerance of 1e-5.
A diagnostic Hermitian-inner-product variant reduces residuals to approximately 4e-4 to 8e-4 and returns stable transfer maxima around 1.7 to 1.9 on three independently checked spike scenes.
conclusion: The extreme BEM values are numerical artifacts from an unstable and unchecked iterative solve, not physical transfer resonances and not a free-field normalization failure.
required_before_regeneration: Return iteration count and residual from every solve.
Reject or retry any frequency whose residual exceeds an agreed threshold.
Add a preconditioner or a robust fallback because the corrected unpreconditioned solver can stagnate around residual 1e-4.
Verify repeatability on spiking and ordinary general/enclosed scenes before regenerating any BEM labels.
